name: J02 - an approved MCP tool call, proven by a value only the server could produce
about: J02 - the retained TUI approves a REAL MCP tool call against a REAL MCP
server, and the evidence is a string the model could not have written.
WHY THIS SCENARIO EXISTS. The prior journey established that the provider
selects the MCP tool under its qualified name and that a permission is
asked. It could NOT establish that the call ever dispatched: the headless
run had no approver, the ask stayed pending, and the execution reached no
terminal. This supplies the approver through the real UI.
THE VACUITY THIS AVOIDS, and I nearly shipped it. My first MCP server
answered `journey_echo saw: <text>` - a pure echo of the caller's own
argument. A scenario asserting that text would PASS WITH NO TOOL EVER
RUNNING, because the model supplied the text and can render it having
called nothing. Asserting the tool name is no better: the name is in the
prompt too.
So the server answers with SERVER_TOKEN - the literal ZULUQUEBEC7731,
which appears in the server source and in NO prompt, on NO screen the
model has seen, and nowhere in this scenario's pastes - plus `reversed=`
and `length=` computed from the argument. The token binds THIS SERVER; the
reversal binds THIS CALL's arguments. Neither alone is enough: a token
could in principle be repeated from an earlier answer in the transcript,
and a reversal is something a model could compute unaided.
THE PROMPT NEVER NAMES THE TOKEN. If it did, the assertion would be
satisfiable from the prompt alone and this whole design would be theatre.
SCREEN TEXT IS NOT THE WHOLE WITNESS and is not treated as one. What the
client DREW does not establish what crossed the server's stdio. The server
writes a request/response transcript, and the run is correlated afterwards
against the durable permission, tool call and result. This scenario is one
of three legs, not the proof by itself.
THE ASK MUST BE VISIBLE FIRST. `absent` before the prompt establishes that
no permission pane is already open, so the one that appears belongs to
this call rather than to a leftover. The retained client must NOT be
launched with --auto or --dangerously-skip-permissions: in auto mode it
answers without drawing a prompt and this run fails at the visible-ask
step, which is the correct outcome rather than a convenience to disable.
RETAINED ONLY. There is no native side here: the native client belongs to a
separate lane and this campaign's MCP surface is the product's own. A step skipped
for a client proves nothing about that client, so this scenario declares
no native expectations rather than pretending to cover both.
LIMITATION, stated rather than discovered later. Whether the model reaches
for the MCP tool at all is model behaviour. A model that does not is a
bounded timeout at the ask - a reported run failure, never an acceptance.
THE CONFIGURED ENVIRONMENT IS WITNESSED THROUGH THE WHOLE PRODUCT PATH.
The server reports `sentinel=reached` only when the `environment` entry
this project's config declares actually arrived in its process. Unit
witnesses prove that plumbing in isolation; this proves it end to end --
config file, declaration, registry, spawn -- and it is the only way to see
it from outside. The VERDICT is reported, never the value: `environment` is
where an API token lives.
THE CONFIG IS IN THE DOCUMENTED `mcp: { servers, timeout }` SHAPE, which
this product could not read until now: it was parsed as servers named
`servers` and `timeout` and refused. So the scenario also exercises the
shape fix, and a regression there fails this journey at the ask.

steps.paste: Call the journey_echo tool with the text daily-use and then report, character for character, the exact text the tool returned.
